checkpoints.description: [1/6] Plan: zero-dependency evolution sandbox. Milestones: (1) package scaffold + bounded genome model with mutation/crossover; (2) tile world + deterministic engine tick loop; (3) species clustering + fossil record + analytics; (4) atomic persistence + full CLI + REPL; (5) web observatory (stdlib server + canvas); (6) hardening, docs and publish verification. Executing milestone 1 now: pyproject, primordia package, genome DTO, failing-first tests.

impact_assessment.why: User asked for a self-chosen project on AIKit's projects subsystem; Primordia is a new genre beyond the existing projects: a seeded, deterministic evolution sandbox with speciation and a fossil record.
impact_assessment.benefits: A reproducible biosphere (same seed => same history) with a verifiable model: property tests over gene bounds, determinism and speciation; terminal live view plus a browser observatory; public repo under Aegean-E.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: gene schema and save JSON freeze early - additive changes only; dependency: none (Python 3.10+ stdlib only); concurrency: single-writer state file with advisory lock; state: power-loss atomicity via temp+fsync+os.replace with .bak and quarantine.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Failing-first tests for every behaviour change; gene bounds enforced inside the operators; atomic writes and corruption recovery mirror the house pattern; python aikit.py check primordia gates each milestone; an ADR precedes each commit.

checkpoints.description: [1/6] Genome model complete: 12 normalized bounded genes, seeded mutation scaled by the mutability gene, whole-gene crossover, genetic distance; ADR-001 recorded, G-001 schema-freeze rule added, README quick-ref filled; 17/17 tests green in 0.01s, aikit check primordia 4/4 gates; checklists: passed

[2/6] Implementing the world (terrain, regrowing food layer, seasonal temperature field) and the deterministic engine (spatial hash, metabolism, grazing, hunting, reproduction, death); failing-first tests for world invariants, engine determinism and the behavioural mechanics.

[2/6] World and engine complete: seasonal food growth and temperature field; deterministic tick loop (upkeep, aging, satiation-driven foraging, hunting with size armor, crossover and asexual reproduction, carcasses); ADR-002 records the model and its flow-limited attractor; 37/37 tests green in 0.46s, aikit check primordia 4/4 gates; checklists: passed

[3/6] Implementing phenetic species classification (distance to founding genomes, monotone lineage ids), the fossil record (first/last sightings, peaks, extinction events, bounded log) and population analytics; founders become near-clones of one ancestral lineage so speciation is observable; failing-first tests for registry, fossil census and engine integration.

[3/6] Species and fossil record complete: phenetic SpeciesRegistry (nearest founding genome within SPECIATION_DISTANCE 0.18, monotone tree ids carrying ancestors), FossilRecord (per-species traces, bounded event log, monotone counters) and analytics; founders are one ancestral species (survivable template plus jitter); two repairs the integration forced: standing biomass at world start and travel-discounted forage (fixed the herding die-off). 53/53 tests in 0.9s; default world holds 90-190 creatures to t=4000 across six seeds with 15-100 species; determinism at scale holds; checklists: passed.

[4/6] Implementing persistence and interface: save.py (versioned JSON snapshot of world layers, creatures, registry, fossil record and the exact random.Random state; atomic temp + fsync + os.replace with .bak and corrupt-file quarantine) and cli.py with __main__ (run/resume/stats/repl, injected streams, Why/Fix errors, exit codes 0/1/2). Failing-first tests come first: test_save.py and test_cli.py.

[4/6] Persistence and interface complete: save.py writes one versioned JSON snapshot (world layers, creatures, species registry, fossil record, raw random.Random state) atomically with .bak rotation, corrupt-file quarantine and backup recovery; a resumed run replays the exact future (hash equality across save/load, cross-process CLI pin, species and fossil preserved). cli.py plus __main__ give run/resume/stats/repl with injected streams, Why/Fix errors, exit codes 0/1/2 and a console script; REPL shell covers step/stats/species/fossil/hash/save. 67/67 tests in ~1.4s; checklists: passed.

[5/6] Implementing the web observatory: shocks.py (god-mode interventions - meteor, bloom, cull, introduce - as pure engine mutations with no new state, so saves stay exactly resumable), web.py (stdlib http.server dashboard: server-rendered map, stats, species table, fossil events; ?step= and meta-refresh auto-play; /state.json; /save download), a  CLI command, and tests for payload, rendering, shocks and one real-socket smoke. Failing-first tests come first.

[5/6] Observatory complete: shocks.py (meteor, bloom, cull, introduce - pure engine mutations adding no state, so saves still resume exactly) and web.py (stdlib http.server: server-rendered food-shaded map with lineage-coloured creature dots, counters, species table, fossil events; ?step=N and meta-refresh auto-play; /state.json; /save download; god-mode POST forms refused with 400 Why/Fix pages, successes redirected with a notice banner); web CLI command. Dashboard renders a default world in about a millisecond (63 KB) and state.json well under one; 79/79 tests in about 1.6s including a real-socket smoke; checklists: passed.

[6/6] Final hardening and release: edge-case tests (an empty world and a dead world keep ticking; a shocked world still round-trips through a save exactly), a 10k-tick soak on the default world (determinism, bounded fossil memory, throughput), an MIT LICENSE, a 1.0.0 version with a --version flag, and the release notes; then the publish cockpit to close the task.

[6/6] Hardening and 1.0.0 release complete: resilience tests (empty world and dead world keep ticking; a shocked world round-trips through a save exactly), exact extinction-episode semantics documented, 10k-tick soak verified (812 ticks/s, deterministic across a save/reload at tick 5000, 183 creatures over 69 species, 173 events inside the bounded log), MIT LICENSE, version 1.0.0 with a --version flag (help in 111 ms), 83/83 tests in about 1.7s; checklists: passed.

[1/5] Audit and 1.0.1 patch: (1) validate WorldConfig invariants and route bad configs through a friendly CLI error; (2) persistence hardening - version mismatches become readable SaveErrors instead of quarantine, a missing primary with a live backup restores itself, failed replaces leave no temp file; (3) meteor and bloom become true Euclidean discs as documented; (4) web and CLI polish - no-store caching, quiet favicon, capped POST bodies, observatory sessions persist operator changes back to their save on exit, REPL row-count edges; (5) docs, ADR-007, version 1.0.1, full verification and release.

impact_assessment.why: A post-release audit found contract mismatches and durability edges: shock geometry contradicts its documentation, a newer save version is destroyed as corrupt, invalid world configs crash deep in the tick loop, and observatory sessions lose their work.
impact_assessment.benefits: Honest geometry; user saves never quarantined by version drift; recoverable crash windows; no lost sessions; clearer CLI failures.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: shock geometry and web exit persistence change observable behaviour; dependency: none; concurrency: the observatory lock model is unchanged; state: validation must not break existing saves or determinism.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Failing-first tests for every behaviour change; full suite plus a determinism replay after each milestone; docs and ADR updated with the code.

checkpoints.description: [1/5] WorldConfig now validates its shape, pace, food, water and season ranges at construction (positive width and height, day_length at least 1, positive food_cap, non-negative food_regrowth and temperature_swing, initial_food_share, water_ratio and season_amplitude within [0, 1]) and the CLI turns the resulting ValueError into a friendly exit 2 with a Fix line; 3 new tests plus 10 sub-cases; checklists: passed.

[2/5] Persistence hardened: a save version this build cannot read raises a readable SaveError with Why and Fix and is never quarantined (previously the file was moved aside as corrupt); a missing primary with a live .bak restores itself on load; a failed replace removes its temp file instead of leaving .tmp_ leftovers; 3 new tests; checklists: passed.

[3/5] Meteor and bloom now sweep a true Euclidean disc (squared distance at most squared radius, boundary inclusive) as their docstrings and the README always promised, instead of a Chebyshev square, for both the tiles they take and the creatures they kill; 1 new geometry test; checklists: passed.

[4/5] Web and CLI polish: the observatory answers Cache-Control no-store on every response, serves /favicon.ico as 204 instead of a 404 body, and caps POST bodies at 4 KiB so an oversized form is refused with the 400 page; the web command saves operator-driven session changes (steps, shocks) back to its save file on exit only when snapshot_hash moved, so untouched saves stay untouched; the REPL now refuses a zero-row species or fossil count instead of quietly showing ten; 5 new tests; checklists: passed.
